findings.F1: The two hours after the 21:00 UTC close rise whether or not the coin fell. The hour-20 and hour-21 bars are the two strongest hours of the day (mean 0.000545, t 6.75, n 17403; and 0.000436, t 5.66, n 17417). The 2-hour return is positive in every coin (0.00082 to 0.00114, t 3.1 to 4.7, about 2750 cases each) and in 79 % of windows. It also holds after rises: the top vol-scaled-return decile gives 0.0017 (t 4.1, n 1641), and the Spearman correlation between the size of a rise and the return is -0.004.
findings.F2: That 2-hour rise after 21:00 grows with the coin's 7-day hourly volatility. By per-coin volatility quartile it is 0.00030 (t 2.35), 0.00079 (t 4.87), 0.00079 (t 3.64) and 0.00211 (t 6.49), about 4100 cases each.
findings.F3: The rise after 21:00 follows the size of the past 24-hour move, not its sign. By quintile of the absolute vol-scaled 24-hour return it is 0.00109, 0.00044, 0.00034, 0.00142 and 0.00169 (top quintile t 5.47, n 3281). After falls, the fall's depth correlates only weakly with the return (Spearman 0.061).
findings.F4: The book loses although the timing is real. Summed gross position gains of 5.34 are outweighed by summed fees of -7.81, and per-trade gross P/L runs from +0.09 % (BTC) to -0.07 % (XRP) against about 0.1 % of commission per trade. The book's daily Sharpe is -0.67 and its mean daily return is -0.00014.
findings.F5: Over the next 24 hours, the coin's past 24-hour vol-scaled return predicts a reversal. The OLS slope is -0.0019 (t -4.72, n 15950, non-overlapping daily cases). The lowest vol-scaled-return quintile is followed by roughly +0.004 to +0.007 over 24 hours, the highest by -0.0017 to +0.0002.
findings.F6: Days whose 24-hour move was spread evenly across hours are followed by larger 3-day returns than days dominated by one hour, whatever the move's direction. Grouped by the share of the day's absolute hourly moves taken by the largest hour, the next 72-hour return is 0.0061 (t 5.13), 0.0040 (t 3.42) and 0.0001 (t 0.11), n about 5317 each. High minus low is -0.0060, Welch t -3.72. Over 24 hours the same gap is weaker (t -1.39).
findings.F7: Two other hours fall consistently across the pooled coins: the hour-13 bar (-0.000356, t -3.80) and the hour-2 bar (-0.000277, t -3.80), each with about 17400 cases.

ideas.idea: Each coin rises over the two hours after 21:00 UTC, and the higher its 7-day hourly volatility at that close, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would lean long into the 21:00 UTC close with size scaled up by the coin's recent volatility, whatever its 24-hour direction, because the move is too small to pay costs in calm coins.
ideas.name: volatility-scaled evening UTC rise

ideas.idea: The deeper a coin's 24-hour return falls in units of its 7-day hourly volatility, the larger its rise over the next 24 hours.
ideas.consequence: A trader would buy coins after steep vol-scaled daily drops and hold for a day, a horizon long enough for the move to clear the round-trip cost.
ideas.name: daily vol-scaled drop reversal

ideas.idea: The more evenly a coin's absolute hourly moves over the past 24 hours are spread across the hours, the larger its rise over the next 3 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would favour long exposure after days of evenly spread hourly moves and refuse it after days dominated by a single violent hour.
ideas.name: even-step days precede gains
